hoogle:src/General/Web.hs:178:Cross-Site.label: ambiguous
hoogle:src/General/Web.hs:178:Cross-Site.reason: The text of an exception raised while answering the request is written as a 500 body with no content type. Query parsing returns errors as values rather than throwing, so the text is normally an internal error, but an exception that quoted the request would be reflected without a declared type; a browser may sniff it. hoogle:src/General/Web.hs:180:path-trave.label: FP

yesod:yesod-auth/Yesod/Auth/Email.hs:959.vuln: Password hashed with a fast general-purpose hash
yesod:yesod-auth/Yesod/Auth/Email.hs:959.label: FP
yesod:yesod-auth/Yesod/Auth/Email.hs:959.reason: `saltPass'` is the legacy MD5 verifier kept for passwords hashed before PasswordStore: `isValidPass ct salted = PS.verifyPassword .. || isValidPass' ct salted`, and `isValidPass'` only compares `salted == saltPass' salt clear`; `saltPass` (the one that stores) uses `PS.makePassword`. The migration shape the rule recognises, except that the KDF is `Yesod.Auth.Util.PasswordStore`, a vendored copy of the password-store package under another module name, and the KDF sits one hop ABOVE the comparing function. Not fixed this round: recognising a vendored KDF module needs its construction read (STRef loop, not `iterate`).

graphql-engine:server/src-lib/Hasura/Ser.label: ambiguous
graphql-engine:server/src-lib/Hasura/Ser.reason: `readProcessWithExitCode "pg_dump" opts` with `opts` taken from the request body (`prbOpts`): the pg_dump API is an admin-only endpoint whose documented feature is passing pg_dump options; an admin can pass any option.
